description: Use case: the inheritance split of a securities depot into the parent portfolio and two child portfolios, respecting the lot sizes, as shown on the page 'Portfolio Split Calculator' (src/test/resources/web/html/use_cases/portfolio_split_calculator_sample.html). The inputs are the holdings, prices, lot sizes and exchange rates of the synthetic bank report (portfolio_report.json), the instruments and their issuers (portfolio_instruments.json) and the 30 / 35 / 35 split agreement with the agreed allocation of the two Lindt & Sprüngli holdings (portfolio_split_parameters_sample.json). The holdings are walked from the largest unit value times lot size to the smallest: the first child gets its target share of the holding value minus the deviation carried in from the holdings before, rounded to the lot size; the second child gets the same count, because both target shares are equal; the parent keeps the remainder, so every holding is conserved exactly; and the cash at the end, divisible to 0.01, closes the remaining drift to below one centime. The holding values, the remainder of the parent, the target values and the final split deviation are formulas of this file reproduced by the calc-validation; the lot value, the target, the count of each beneficiary and the cumulative deviation of every row of the walk are formulas too, which read the deviation of the row before with the operand prior along the is follower of chain of the holdings. The totals per kind of holding, the realised value and the realised share are stored as modelled values, because a formula cannot sum over the rows of the walk yet. The calculator triples of the base phrase portfolio split describe the page, so the system view Calculator shows the example portfolio split like the PV lifetime balance. ADDITIONALLY NEEDED, marked PROPOSED NEW ELEMENT in the keyword descriptions of calculator_keywords.json and described in docs/json_structure.md: (1) a repeated input 'calculator repeat' for the add and remove of children, whose result and walk columns follow the instances of child portfolio; (2) a checkbox field 'calculator checkbox' for mirror the children and split cash; (3) a read only field 'calculator read only' for the target weight of the parent; (4) a conditional text 'calculator warning' for the weight checks; (5) one collapsed section per detail table 'calculator section'; (6) number fields in a detail table 'calculator editable' for the holdings; (7) a column 'calculator phrase column' that shows the currency of the numbers of a holding; (8) the walk table parts 'calculator row number' and the order of the rows by the verb is ranked by to lot value; (9) the column colours 'calculator colour'; (10) the notes list 'calculator note'; (11) a check table 'calculator check' of the expected allocations of the split agreement; (12) a line diagram 'calculator diagram' of the cumulative deviation; (13) the buttons 'calculator file import', 'calculator download', 'calculator printable report' and 'calculator copy'; (14) 'calculator page independent' for the holdings, the walk, the exchange rates and the check, whose numbers do not have the page phrase; (15) the detail table rows over several levels of is a and is part of, e.g. LISP is a stock is a holding is part of split walk, and a cell that skips the numbers of another column, so that the count of a child is not taken for its cumulative deviation; (16) the sum over the rows of the walk for the totals per kind of holding and the realised value; (17) the total of the realised portfolio value, which a value with realised value would let the split deviation formula calculate again for the whole depot; (18) a rounding rule for a tie, because the stored targets of SCHP, STMN, ABBN and CHF cash are just below the tie to keep the counts of the sample, and the calculation of the walk in the browser after an input change.

triples.name: portfolio split note rule
triples.description: A child's target is its weight times the position value, minus the deviation carried in from earlier positions. That target in units is rounded to the nearest round lot. With mirroring on, every child receives the first child's count. If the rounded counts together exceed the position, every child gets at most an equal part in round lots. The parent gets the rest, so every original position is conserved exactly.

triples.name: portfolio split note deviation
triples.description: The carried deviation is the realised value minus the plain weighted value over all positions split so far, kept per child. It is subtracted once from the next target; it is not added again per step.

triples.name: portfolio split note order
triples.description: LISP has a single unit of CHF 117,000. Rounding 3.5 shares to 4 gives the first child CHF 58,500 too much; the next positions take that back. With the sample data the stocks and bonds bring the drift down to about CHF 13 per child; splitting the cash then closes the gap to below one centime.

formulas.description: the market value of a stock holding: the shares times the stock price

formulas.name: bond holding value
formulas.description: the market value of a bond holding in its own currency: the face value times the bond price in percent of the face value

formulas.name: foreign bond holding value
formulas.description: the market value in CHF of a bond in another currency: the face value times the bond price times the exchange rate

formulas.name: foreign cash holding value
formulas.description: the value in CHF of a cash holding in another currency: the amount times the exchange rate

formulas.name: CHF cash holding value
formulas.description: the value in CHF of the cash holding in CHF: the amount itself, because it needs no exchange rate

formulas.name: lot value of a holding
formulas.description: the value of one lot of a holding: its unit value times its lot size; the walk visits the holdings from the largest lot value to the smallest

formulas.name: walk count of the parent
formulas.description: the parent keeps what is left of a holding after both children have been served, so that every original holding is conserved exactly
formulas.expression: "split count" = "original" - "split count","first child portfolio" - "split count","second child portfolio"

formulas.name: target value of a beneficiary
formulas.description: the CHF amount a beneficiary should receive: the portfolio value times the agreed target share

formulas.name: target share excess formula
formulas.description: how much the target shares of the children exceed the whole portfolio; above zero the page shows a warning
formulas.expression: "target share excess" = "first child portfolio" + "second child portfolio" - "original"

formulas.name: target share difference formula
formulas.description: how much the target shares of the children differ while mirroring is asked; above zero the page shows a warning
formulas.expression: "target share difference" = "mirror" * ( max( "first child portfolio" ; "second child portfolio" ) - min( "first child portfolio" ; "second child portfolio" ) )

formulas.name: unit value of a holding
formulas.description: the value of one unit of a holding: its value divided by its original quantity

formulas.name: walk target of a child
formulas.description: the units that a child should receive of a holding: its target share of the holding value minus the deviation carried in from the row before

formulas.name: walk count of the first child
formulas.description: the target of the first child rounded to the lot size, at most the whole holding
formulas.expression: "split count" = min( max( round( "target quantity" / "lot size" ) * "lot size" ; 0 ) ; "original" )

formulas.name: walk count of the second child
formulas.description: the count of the first child while mirroring is asked, else the target of the second child rounded to the lot size, at most the whole holding
formulas.expression: "split count" = if( "mirror" = 1 ; "split count","first child portfolio" ; min( max( round( "target quantity","second child portfolio" / "lot size" ) * "lot size" ; 0 ) ; "original" ) )

formulas.name: walk deviation of a child
formulas.description: the deviation carried in from the row before plus what the child receives of this holding minus its target share of the holding value
formulas.expression: "cumulative deviation" = "cumulative deviation","prior" + "split count" * "unit value" - "target share" * "holding value"

formulas.name: split deviation formula
formulas.description: how much a beneficiary receives more or less than the target after the rounding to the lot sizes
